title: On the Measure of Intelligence
methodology: Formal definition of general intelligence via Algorithmic Information Theory (AIT), separating task-specific skill from skill-acquisition efficiency, plus construction of the Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) grounded in Core Knowledge priors.
main_findings: Static benchmark skill can be arbitrarily inflated by pre-encoded priors or massive training corpora without increasing generalization power. General intelligence is formally the efficiency with which a learner converts bounded prior knowledge plus small experience into broad out-of-distribution skill.
limitations: AIT quantities (Kolmogorov/Solomonoff complexity) are uncomputable in general and must be approximated empirically on finite task distributions.
relevance_to_agi: Defines our primary evaluation philosophy: architectures must be compared under fixed data/compute/parameter budgets and tested on held-out novel rule induction rather than memorized skill.
potential_implementation: In-context symbolic/grid rule-induction benchmark (few-shot demonstration pairs -> test query) in our evaluation suite.
experimental_validation: Evaluated directly in the Cortex AGI Benchmark Suite (Abstract Rule Induction axis).

title: The Illusion of State in State-Space Models
methodology: Formal circuit-complexity proofs bounding log-precision Transformers and diagonal/scalar-gated State-Space Models (S4, Mamba), paired with empirical state-tracking evaluations on permutation composition (S_5).
main_findings: Both fixed-depth Transformers and diagonal/scalar-gated SSMs lie inside the uniform TC^0 circuit complexity class and provably cannot solve NC^1-complete state-tracking tasks such as composing permutations in S_5 over arbitrary sequence lengths. Input-dependent non-diagonal state transitions (e.g., Householder/Delta products) or depth scaling with sequence/problem complexity escape TC^0.
limitations: Asymptotic log-precision complexity bounds do not characterize finite-length approximation shortcuts, though empirical S_5 tests confirm sharp failure at modest lengths.
relevance_to_agi: Proves mathematically why scaling static-depth Transformers or diagonal SSMs cannot yield general state tracking, code execution, or multi-step world modeling.
potential_implementation: Combine non-commutative Delta-rule state transitions (I - beta k k^T) with adaptive recurrent depth per step.
experimental_validation: Directly tested in Cortex S_5/World-State Tracking benchmark across in-distribution and OOD sequence lengths.

title: Gated Delta Networks: Improving Mamba2 with Delta Rule
methodology: Unifies Mamba2 scalar/selective decay gating with Widrow-Hoff delta-rule associative matrix updates S_t = alpha_t S_{t-1}(I - beta_t k_t k_t^T) + beta_t v_t k_t^T, with hardware-efficient chunkwise WY-representation parallel scan.
main_findings: Decay gating enables rapid wholesale memory erasure (e.g., episode resets) while the delta rule enables targeted key-value overwriting and non-commutative state transitions. Hybrid Gated-DeltaNet + Attention architectures outperform pure Transformers, Mamba2, and un-gated DeltaNet on retrieval and long-context understanding.
limitations: Fixed matrix state capacity O(d_k d_v) per head still suffers graceful interference when unique key-value bindings exceed head rank; still fixed circuit depth per token.
relevance_to_agi: Directly underpins both Qwen3.5-9B (24 Gated-DeltaNet + 8 Attention layers) and fast-weight episodic memory modules.
potential_implementation: Episode-aware and surprise-gated Delta-rule fast-weight memory with decoupled normalized key/query projections.
experimental_validation: Tested via Qwen3.5-9B recurrent state surgery/decay sweeps (harness/) and from-scratch TinyStories & Cortex memory ablations.

title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
methodology: Introduces deep/matrix test-time neural memory updated online via associative prediction-error ('surprise') gradients with momentum and adaptive weight-decay forgetting, paired with sliding/local attention working memory and persistent prompt tokens.
main_findings: Attention serves best as accurate short-term working memory while surprise-driven test-time gradient memory acts as persistent long-term memory, outperforming Transformers and linear RNNs on language modeling and scaling past 2M tokens on needle-in-a-haystack retrieval.
limitations: Chunked parallel training approximates online nonlinear MLP memory updates; does not by itself add adaptive multi-step latent reasoning depth or explicit causal world-model rollouts.
relevance_to_agi: Provides a principled neuro-computational bridge between prediction error (surprise) and fast episodic encoding.
potential_implementation: Surprise-modulated write gate beta_t = sigmoid(w_x x_t + w_err ||v_t - M_{t-1} k_t||) with episode-boundary decay gate.
experimental_validation: Implemented and ablated against un-modulated chunk delta memory on TinyStories recall (0-800 tokens) and Cortex episodic binding.

title: Learning to (Learn at Test Time): RNNs with Expressive Hidden States
methodology: Formulates sequence hidden states as inner-loop parametric learners (TTT-Linear, TTT-MLP) updated via self-supervised reconstruction gradients on each test sequence, meta-trained end-to-end.
main_findings: Demonstrates equivalence between 1-step linear inner gradient descent and linear attention, while expressive inner models (MLP/LayerNorm + multi-step gradient updates) continually reduce perplexity with context length. TTT-Discover (2026) extends test-time RL updates to open scientific/algorithmic optimization.
limitations: Higher per-token FLOPs and custom kernel requirements when inner learners are multi-layer MLPs; naive test-time updates without regularization risk drift over very long non-stationary streams.
relevance_to_agi: Unifies sequence state tracking and continual test-time adaptation into a single bi-level optimization principle.
potential_implementation: Fast-weight inner-loop adaptation module updated via self-supervised prediction error during inference.
experimental_validation: Tested in Cortex Test-Time Continual Adaptation & Rule Shift experiments.

title: Scaling up Test-Time Compute with Latent Reasoning: A Recurrent Depth Approach
methodology: Pretrains a 3.5B language model (Huginn) with a prelude encoder, a weight-tied recurrent core unrolled for randomized iteration counts r during training (with input-anchoring adapter injecting prelude state at every recurrent step), and a coda decoder.
main_findings: Latent recurrent depth scales test-time reasoning compute continuously without requiring verbalized Chain-of-Thought tokens or specialized CoT data, improving math, coding, and logical reasoning up to the effective compute of much larger models while supporting per-token adaptive halting.
limitations: Without input-anchoring, naive looping diverges or collapses to trivial fixed points; standard next-token loss only backpropagates through truncated recurrent steps.
relevance_to_agi: Demonstrates that non-verbal latent iterative computation breaks the fixed-depth feedforward bottleneck of standard Transformers.
potential_implementation: Input-anchored recurrent core z^{(k+1)} = Core(Adapter([x_enc, z^{(k)}]) + step_emb_k) trained with randomized recurrence depth and halting/confidence supervision.
experimental_validation: Tested both zero-shot on Qwen3.5-9B (showing un-trained looping degrades PPL) and trained from scratch in lab/ & cortex/.

title: Hierarchical Reasoning Model
methodology: Couples a slow high-level recurrent module and fast low-level recurrent module with deep supervision and adaptive computation halting on Sudoku, Maze, and ARC-AGI (27M params).
main_findings: Achieves strong small-model puzzle solving (32% semi-private ARC-AGI-1), demonstrating deep latent recurrence outperforms CoT on symbolic/spatial constraint satisfaction. Crucially, independent ARC Prize ablations showed the iterative outer-loop refinement and deep supervision—rather than two-module hierarchy—drove almost all gains.
limitations: 2% on ARC-AGI-2; heavy reliance on task-specific augmentations; complex two-frequency hierarchy proved largely redundant under rigorous ablation.
relevance_to_agi: Exemplifies why independent ablation is mandatory in AGI research: architectural complexity must earn its keep over simpler mechanisms.
potential_implementation: Deeply-supervised iterative latent-and-answer refinement rather than unverified multi-module complexity.
experimental_validation: Directly informs our ablation between single-core iterative refinement (TRM-style) vs over-parameterized hierarchies.

title: Less is More: Recursive Reasoning with Tiny Networks
methodology: Replaces HRM's 27M dual-hierarchy with a single 2-layer, 7M-parameter recursive network (Tiny Recursive Model, TRM) that alternates n latent updates z <- f(x, y, z) and K answer updates y <- g(y, z) with deep supervision and learned halting.
main_findings: Outperforms 27M HRM on Sudoku, Maze, ARC-AGI-1 (45% vs 41%), and ARC-AGI-2 (8% vs 2%) using 4x fewer parameters, proving recursive self-correction of (latent z, candidate output y) anchored to input x is a potent, parameter-efficient reasoning primitive.
limitations: Still trained on static puzzle distributions without persistent cross-episode fast-weight memory or action-conditioned world models.
relevance_to_agi: Validates explicit iterative error-correction dynamics (conditioning latent updates on both input x and current candidate hypothesis y).
potential_implementation: Hypothesis-refinement loop in Cortex Reasoning Engine: iteratively updating latent workspace z and candidate prediction y gated by self-evaluated confidence.
experimental_validation: Evaluated directly on Compositional Reasoning, State Tracking, and Abstract Grid Rule Induction in Cortex.

title: The Tolman-Eichenbaum Machine: Unifying Space and Relational Memory through Generalization in the Hippocampal Formation
methodology: Computational neuroscience model factorizing structural transition algebra (medial entorhinal cortex, slow weights) from rapid Hebbian/attractor sensory-structural binding (hippocampus, fast weights) trained via predictive sequence learning.
main_findings: Spontaneously develops grid, border, band, place, and landmark cell representations and explains zero-shot structural transfer ('remapping with preserved relational structure') across spatial and abstract relational graphs (e.g., family trees).
limitations: Trained on small discrete graph worlds; standard Hebbian attractors saturate faster than delta-rule orthogonalized updates.
relevance_to_agi: Provides biological proof-of-principle that separating slow structural transition rules from fast episodic variable binding enables systematic relational generalization.
potential_implementation: Decouple slow structural transition/reasoning weights from fast Delta-rule variable-binding memory so abstract rules transfer zero-shot to novel entities.
experimental_validation: Tested in Cortex Relational Binding & Novel-Symbol Zero-Shot Transfer benchmark.

title: Loss of Plasticity in Deep Continual Learning
methodology: Long-horizon continual supervised (Continual ImageNet) and reinforcement learning experiments across hundreds of task shifts, measuring dormant units, weight growth, effective rank collapse, and continual backpropagation.
main_findings: Standard backpropagation + Adam progressively loses the ability to learn new tasks (plasticity collapse) due to weight magnitude inflation, dead/dormant neurons, and representation rank collapse. Continual backpropagation (selectively reinitializing lowest-utility units) and shrink-and-perturb / L2 regenerative regularization sustain plasticity indefinitely.
limitations: Maintaining plasticity alone solves forward learning on new tasks, not backward retention (catastrophic forgetting), which additionally requires memory separation or replay.
relevance_to_agi: Proves continual lifelong learning has TWO dual failure modes: catastrophic forgetting (too plastic) AND loss of plasticity (too rigid).
potential_implementation: Combine (a) fast episodic memory + task-conditioned replay consolidation (preventing forgetting) with (b) weight-norm/shrink-and-perturb plasticity preservation.
experimental_validation: Directly tested in Cortex Continual Multi-Phase Learning benchmark measuring both Backward Transfer (forgetting) and Forward Plasticity.

title: Mastering Diverse Control Tasks through World Models
methodology: Recurrent State-Space World Model (RSSM) with discrete categorical latents, symlog/percentile return normalization, KL balancing, and actor-critic policy optimization on imagined latent rollouts across 150+ tasks.
main_findings: Single fixed-hyperparameter world-model architecture masters 150+ diverse environments and collects diamonds in Minecraft from scratch by planning in imagined latent trajectories.
limitations: Pure actor-critic policy amortization without explicit tree/MPC search at decision time can still misstep on sharp combinatorial traps (e.g., Sokoban/Key-Door dead ends).
relevance_to_agi: Establishes scale-invariant latent world models (predicting next latent state + reward + continuation) as a domain-general foundation for autonomous agency.
potential_implementation: Normalized latent world-model transition + reward/value predictor in Cortex coupled with decision-time lookahead rollout planning.
experimental_validation: Tested in Cortex Key-Door-Trap POMDP Planning benchmark comparing reactive policy vs learned World-Model MPC/Tree Lookahead.

title: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models Enable Understanding, Prediction and Planning
venue: arXiv:2506.09985 (building on LeCun 2022, A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence)
methodology: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture pre-trained on 1M+ hours of unlabeled video by predicting masked target latent representations (EMA target encoder, avoiding pixel-level generative collapse), followed by lightweight action-conditioned latent world-model post-training.
main_findings: Predicting in abstract representation space (JEPA) rather than raw observation space filters irrelevant surface noise and enables zero-shot physical robot manipulation via latent trajectory optimization toward goal embeddings.
limitations: Requires anti-collapse target mechanisms (EMA stop-gradient or variance-covariance regularization); continuous visual latents alone struggle with discrete symbolic logic without reasoning recurrence.
relevance_to_agi: Validates representation-space predictive world modeling (L_pred = ||Pred(z_t, a_t) - sg(z_{t+1})||) over pure surface-token/pixel reconstruction.
potential_implementation: EMA/stop-gradient auxiliary latent next-state prediction objective inside Cortex World-Model Subsystem, whose prediction error simultaneously drives the surprise gate for episodic memory.
experimental_validation: Ablated in both TinyStories latent-prediction experiments and Cortex World-Model Planning.

title: Toward Causal Representation Learning
methodology: Synthesizes Pearl's structural causal models (SCMs) with deep representation learning via the Independent Causal Mechanisms (ICM) principle and sparse mechanism shift hypothesis.
main_findings: Observational statistical models estimate P(Y|X) and systematically fail under confounding and intervention P(Y|do(X=x)). Factorization into modular, sparsely interacting causal mechanisms allows localized updates under intervention (severing incoming parent links of do-variables) and rapid adaptation under sparse distribution shifts.
limitations: Causal graph identifiability from purely observational i.i.d. data is impossible without interventional data, temporal/structural constraints, or sparse mechanism shifts.
relevance_to_agi: Explains why correlation-trained foundation models hallucinate causal effects under confounded observations and how interventional conditioning fixes it.
potential_implementation: Explicit operator/graph-state representation supporting interventional operator semantics (severing causal parents of intervened nodes during iterative message passing / latent rollout).
experimental_validation: Evaluated in Cortex Confounded Causal Reasoning benchmark (P(Y|X=x) vs P(Y|do(X=x)) on unseen confounded DAGs).

title: Predictive Coding in the Visual Cortex: A Functional Interpretation of Some Extra-Classical Receptive-Field Effects
venue: Nature Neuroscience 2(1), 79-87 (and Friston 2010, Free-Energy Principle, Nature Reviews Neuroscience)
methodology: Hierarchical generative cortical circuit in which top-down feedback carries predictions of lower-level activity and feedforward pathways propagate only residual prediction errors to iteratively infer latent causes.
main_findings: Iterative prediction-error minimization explains extra-classical cortical phenomena (end-stopping, surprise amplification, familiarity suppression) and unifies perception, inference, and learning around a single local error currency.
limitations: Exact bi-directional settling dynamics can be slow compared to amortized feedforward pass unless hybridized: fast amortized feedforward sweep + k-step top-down residual refinement.
relevance_to_agi: Provides a single unifying signal—prediction error / epistemic surprise—linking (1) memory encoding strength, (2) adaptive reasoning iterations, and (3) world-model learning.
potential_implementation: Amortized encoder + top-down iterative residual error feedback + surprise-driven fast-weight gating.
experimental_validation: Tested via top-down feedback experiments on Qwen3.5-9B and trained end-to-end in Cortex.

title: Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents
methodology: Replaces intractable formal proof requirements of Schmidhuber's Godel Machine with an open-ended quality-diversity archive of self-modifying systems validated empirically on held-out benchmarks in sandboxed environments.
main_findings: Maintaining a branching archive of diverse ancestral checkpoints (rather than greedily overwriting a single lineage) prevents local-optima trapping and catastrophic self-modification collapse, producing cumulative measurable capability gains.
limitations: Vulnerable to benchmark Goodharting if validation suites are narrow or leaked; bounded by underlying base model priors unless architectural/learning primitives also evolve.
relevance_to_agi: Defines a safe, reversible, version-controlled engineering protocol for recursive architectural/algorithmic self-improvement.
potential_implementation: Archive-backed autonomous hypothesis & hyperparameter/architecture mutation loop in Cortex with strict train/val/OOD-test separation and automatic rollback on regression.
experimental_validation: Executed in our autonomous architecture refinement cycles with full checkpoint lineage and held-out OOD verification.
